cells.tense: You are holding much of what you perceive, and it is feeding what you tend.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Say what you notice growing here before anyone asks — the piece only you've caught, plainly, once, without pushing it.
cells.core:
A lot has come clear to you about what you're tending, and the clarity isn't crowding it. You can tell what the second week needs without running it, and check again at the end without losing anything, because there is room in what you notice. That's the part to lean on. Your read and the work sit level, and nothing is enforced on either side.
Put the frame on the table before anyone asks. Choose one piece of what you notice — the piece only you have caught — and tell the person or people in it, plainly, once, without pushing. Handed over, it stops being a private read and becomes something the growing thing can be organised around.
cells.sheetLine: You can see it plainly, and the seeing is company.
cells.place: in the middle of care for what is growing

cells.tense: You will have settled how it turns out before it has had a chance to show you.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Name one outcome for this thing to yourself, and hold that bearing for three days — then check once whose choice it was.
cells.core:
Under this much sight, everything you care for is being mapped forward. You know where it's headed next week, what a wrong turn will cost, which version of it will disappoint you — and care for it has turned into managing a future that hasn't arrived. Knowing comes before the thing has shown itself and steers, and the growing thing doesn't get to find its own way. That pre-deciding is the bend, and the way through is to commit to one heading on purpose rather than holding every possible one.
Name one outcome for this thing to yourself, and hold that bearing for three days. Then check once whose choice it was.
cells.sheetLine: You've mapped the ending before the thing could arrive.
cells.place: in the middle of care for what is growing

cells.tense: What you once saw clearly was real, and you still stand as if the door to it were ahead of you.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Bring one other person into this by your own hand — do a piece of the work together, and stay past the part you'd leave.
cells.core:
You can't quite believe what you noticed anymore. It came in once, the clear sense of what was developing and which way it needed to go, and now you can't tell whether that was real or a story you made. Not because it left — you're keeping it away from anything that could confirm it, your hands stay off, and you leave before anything shows. Seen alongside someone, it lands without argument. Right now nothing is landing on purpose.
Bring one other person into this by your own hand — sit with them and do a small piece of the work together, one you'd normally hand off or abandon, and stay with them past the point you'd leave. Shared, it carries a shape.
cells.sheetLine: You saw something once. You've been standing away from it.
cells.place: in the middle of care for what is growing

cells.tense: Some part of you has already weighed what is fair here, and you keep deciding it isn't your call.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Pick something you quietly sense is owed here — a hand, a share of the work you carry — and do it this week where nobody is watching.
cells.core:
The care you give has a moral shape — you sense what's fair with the people in this, what's owed, who's carrying more than their share. But when the moment comes to act on it, you say the circumstances are unclear, or that it isn't only your call. That sense of what's fair keeps operating; your account of yourself leaves it out, and those close by see only the care, not the judgment inside it.
Pick something you quietly sense is owed here — a hand, a share of the work you're carrying, a correction to something small — and do it this week where nobody is watching. That private count is accurate. Act on it once.
cells.sheetLine: You sense what's fair, and you've been keeping it private.
cells.place: in the middle of care for what is growing

attempts.check: The record says the fullness is present and that the balance points toward Assertion, but it never says the person has more knowing than they can bear — the plain, unpressured recognition of what is blooming is my own read and could be wrong. A reader could reasonably say the knowing isn't plentiful in them at all, only ordinary. Each ask survives being wrong: saying the shape out loud, taking one bearing, joining someone in one piece of the work, and following the private sense of what's right all make sense even if the person's knowing is thin. The sentence serving the writer more than the person is any line that makes this sound like a crown rather than a description.
